limitations.text: Machines: Intel Granite Rapids and Graviton 4, reported separately. CPUs order encoders differently: in the study's single-encode runs, Zen 4 and Intel moved encoders by up to ±11 % against Zen 5. No AMD series is in this round.

items.text: On Graviton, half load moves encoders against each other by up to 22 % relative to an idle machine (×1.01-1.23).
Ours and SVT-AV1's fast presets are the most affected; that is the measure, stated, and our encoder's cache sensitivity is open work (T28).

limitations.text: Agreement between machines of one type is assumed. It is checked on every run (V6), and each report states it.

Rates: nothing above 1200 kbps (720p30-equivalent) is measured. A dev diagnosis at 600-4000 kbps (docs/analysis/upper-rates-diagnosis-2026-11-23.md, four 720p pool clips) measured a reversal for our fast presets there: AV1 veryfast +5.4 % and H.264 veryfast +41.9 % against x264 medium.
Slow end: no reference is charted slower than x265 medium, SVT-AV1 M8, libaom cpu8 or libvpx cpu7, so our slowest presets (VVC slow to veryslow) have no reference beside them.

Tuning: our presets are tuned at these rates; no reference is. Screens rank at 150 frames, but changes to rate, keys, cadence or key quality, and every preset bundle's final check, are decided on long windows (nceval.levels, nceval.key_shares): 600 frames with a key every 150, and 900 frames with a key every 300.

In-sample clips: 9 VC-1K clips were lever-ranking sets for every codec on 2026-11-18/19 (the VC-1K headline leaves them out; the full set is shown beside it), and AOM-CTC's 12 low-delay clips are the standards lens ours was developed on (labelled; A2 alone is shown beside it). The rest of VC-1K shares its source with the clips whose problems were chosen.

Start-up: every window starts with a key frame and a full 1 s buffer; each "ours" clip counts once, and only 40 of its 97 clips also have a 600-frame window beside the 150-frame one. Our first key is 0.35-0.58 s of the channel (median) against 0.09-0.21 s for x264, x265 and SVT-AV1 ("ours", c8i); capping it costs ours 5.0-7.8 % J by our own measurement (docs/analysis/first-key-2026-11-25.md). The references' start-up effect is not measured. The site shows each family's first key beside its BD and the 600-frame windows' BD beside the headline.
Timing machines: on c8i "ours", our families and the references were timed on two machines whose start check sets used different clips, so their agreement was not measured.

items.text: the "ours" set was audited once, and read for quality by release measurements on 2026-11-23 to 11-26 while our encoder changed; no lever is recorded as chosen from it;
it has no pan or moving-camera class;
pan, lowlight and drone are thin.

limitations.text: Common set: in BP-4 (both chips) 92 of the 97 clips on "ours" (128 of 137 clip-windows), 99 of 100 on VC-1K (90 of 91 without its in-sample clips) and 34 of 34 on AOM-CTC. On "ours", 8 of the 9 lost clip-windows are lost wholly or partly because our own curves lie above x264 medium's quality range (section 9). Each report lists the lost clips with the reason. Both the common-set and the own-set figures are published.

Thin overlaps and two-point curves count in full since BP-3.14. A BD over a narrow shared range, or through two points, is a weaker estimate than one over four points and a wide range; the reports show each family's overlap so that this is visible.

items.text: variable-frame-rate sources are converted to a constant rate by the pinned ffmpeg (identical input for every encoder);
CrowdRun and OldTownCross carry a standards-only licence notice and are flagged.
one thread, 8-bit, no reordering for everyone; the prediction structure is each encoder's own real-time default (SVT-AV1 runs its 2-level structure, Kvazaar lp-g8d4t1);
scene-cut keys are not uniform: x264 and openh264 choose their own, the other references run without them (section 17, scene_cut);
VVenC is not charted: its rate control is VBR with a look-ahead, so it has no real-time CBR mode, and BP-4 has no Fixed QP mode.

limitations.text: Window: the 150-frame unit includes one key frame.
VMAF v1 at native size is a relative metric, not comparable with published 1080p VMAF.
